title: Blob versioning, soft delete, and Azure Files snapshots
learningObjective: Set up blob versioning, blob and container soft delete, file share snapshots and share soft delete. Pick the right way to recover from an overwrite or a delete.
foundation: Redundancy keeps copies of your data in case hardware fails, but an accidental delete or overwrite is copied everywhere too. Data protection features keep older copies for you.
Blob versioning saves the previous version every time a blob is changed or deleted. Soft delete keeps deleted blobs or containers for a set number of days so you can undelete them.
For Azure Files, share snapshots are read-only point-in-time copies of a whole share, and share soft delete lets you undelete a deleted share.
engineer: Blob versioning: every write or delete saves the old content as a version, with a version ID (a timestamp). The current content is the base blob. To restore, copy an older version over the base blob.
Versioning cost: you pay for each version's unique data. Add lifecycle rules that delete old versions.
Blob soft delete: keeps deleted blobs, snapshots and versions for 1 to 365 days.
Soft delete with versioning on: a delete turns the current content into an older version. Recover by making that version current again.

Soft delete without versioning: a deleted blob is marked soft-deleted, and an overwrite keeps the old content as a soft-deleted snapshot. Recover both with Undelete Blob. Microsoft recommends turning on versioning and soft delete together.
Container soft delete: brings back a deleted container with everything in it (1 to 365 days). Blob soft delete alone does not protect you if the whole container is deleted.
Point-in-time restore: puts block blob containers back to how they were at an earlier time. Needs versioning, change feed and blob soft delete.
Immutable storage (WORM, write once read many): nobody can change or delete the data. Use time-based retention or a legal hold, for compliance.

File share snapshots: read-only copies of the whole share, saving only changes (incremental). Up to 200 per share. Restore single files from the portal or from Windows 'Previous versions'. Azure Backup can take them on a schedule.

File share soft delete: protects whole shares, not single files (1 to 365 days; on by default for new accounts, with 7 days). Deleting a share also deletes its snapshots, so share soft delete protects both. For single files, use snapshots.

animation.caption: Turn protection features on and off, apply overwrites and deletes, then see what is recoverable.

example.title: Protection from ransomware and mistakes
body: The data team turns on versioning, blob soft delete (14 days) and container soft delete (14 days). A lifecycle rule deletes versions older than 90 days to keep cost down.

A script overwrote 2,000 reports with empty files: they restored the older versions. Someone deleted a whole container: container soft delete brought it back. The HR file share gets snapshots every 6 hours through Azure Backup.

prerequisites: A GPv2 account (versioning doesn't work on every account setup; check support for hierarchical namespace accounts)
permissions: Storage Account Contributor, to set up data protection
Storage Blob Data Contributor, to restore versions or undelete blobs
limits: Soft delete keeps items 1 to 365 days
Up to 200 snapshots per file share
portal: Storage account > Data management > Data protection: enable soft delete for blobs (days), soft delete for containers (days), versioning for blobs, point-in-time restore, change feed.
Container > Show deleted blobs / Show versions > Undelete or Make current version.
Storage account > Data storage > Containers > Show deleted containers > Undelete.
File share > Snapshots > + Add snapshot; Restore files. File shares > Show deleted shares > Undelete. Storage account > Data storage > File shares > Soft delete settings.
configuration.cli:
az storage account blob-service-properties update -g rg-data --account-name stcontoso \
  --enable-versioning true --enable-delete-retention true --delete-retention-days 14 \
  --enable-container-delete-retention true --container-delete-retention-days 14
az storage blob undelete --account-name stcontoso -c reports -n q3.csv --auth-mode login
az storage blob list --account-name stcontoso -c reports --include v --auth-mode login -o table
az storage account file-service-properties update -g rg-data --account-name stcontoso --enable-delete-retention true --delete-retention-days 14
az storage share-rm snapshot -g rg-data --storage-account stcontoso --name finance
configuration.powershell:
Update-AzStorageBlobServiceProperty -ResourceGroupName rg-data -StorageAccountName stcontoso -IsVersioningEnabled $true
Enable-AzStorageBlobDeleteRetentionPolicy -ResourceGroupName rg-data -StorageAccountName stcontoso -RetentionDays 14
Enable-AzStorageContainerDeleteRetentionPolicy -ResourceGroupName rg-data -StorageAccountName stcontoso -RetentionDays 14
Update-AzStorageFileServiceProperty -ResourceGroupName rg-data -StorageAccountName stcontoso -EnableShareDeleteRetentionPolicy $true -ShareRetentionDays 14
New-AzRmStorageShare -ResourceGroupName rg-data -StorageAccountName stcontoso -Name finance -Snapshot

lab.objective: Show which feature recovers which kind of mistake.
steps: Versioning & soft delete tab: with everything off, write then overwrite and assess recovery (data lost).
Enable blob soft delete only and repeat (soft-deleted snapshot), then enable versioning instead (previous version).
Add delete-container with container soft delete off, then on.
Azure Files tab: delete a file with no snapshots, take a snapshot, delete again, then delete the share.
expected: Overwrites need versioning or soft delete
Container deletion needs container soft delete
File recovery needs snapshots; share recovery needs share soft delete

validation.text: Recovered data with versioning or soft delete

failureScenarios: Relying on blob soft delete for container deletion
Relying on share soft delete to recover one file
lab.cost: None in the simulation. Versions, soft-deleted data and snapshots are billed for the data they retain.

troubleshooting.symptom: An overwritten blob can't be recovered.
troubleshooting.cause: Versioning and soft delete were both off when it was overwritten, or the retention days had passed.
troubleshooting.fix: Turn on versioning and soft delete. Then restore an older version or undelete the soft-deleted snapshot.

troubleshooting.symptom: Storage cost went up after turning on versioning.
troubleshooting.fix: Add lifecycle rules that move or delete old versions.

troubleshooting.symptom: A deleted container can't be found.
troubleshooting.fix: Turn it on for next time. This container can't be recovered.

troubleshooting.symptom: The share snapshot limit is reached.
troubleshooting.fix: Delete old snapshots, or let Azure Backup manage retention.

comparisons.difference: Adds backup schedules, longer retention and, with vaulted backup, a copy outside the account. It's built on snapshots, versions and soft delete.
Very similar. In S3 a delete adds a 'delete marker' and older versions stay, much like Azure.

misconceptions.reality: No. Deletes are copied to the second region too.

misconceptions.myth: Share soft delete restores single files.
misconceptions.reality: No. It protects whole shares. Use snapshots for single files.
No. Share snapshots only save what changed.

architectureDecisions: Turn on three things on every production account: versioning, blob soft delete and container soft delete.
Keep cost down: use lifecycle rules to delete old versions.
Use Azure Backup for file shares: scheduled snapshots, with retention managed in one place.

steps.label: Mistakes
steps.title: Someone overwrote the budget file, then deleted the folder
body: Without protection, that data is gone. Storage has several undo features, each for a different mistake.

steps.label: Soft delete
steps.title: Soft delete: a recycle bin
body: With blob soft delete, deleted blobs are kept for a retention period (1–365 days) and can be undeleted. Container soft delete does the same for whole containers.

steps.label: Versioning
steps.title: Versioning: every overwrite keeps the old copy
body: With blob versioning on, each write creates a new version and keeps the previous one. Promote an older version to restore it. Versions cost storage, so pair versioning with a lifecycle rule that deletes old versions.

steps.label: Files
steps.title: Azure Files: share soft delete and snapshots
body: Share soft delete keeps a deleted file share for a retention period. Share snapshots are read-only, point-in-time copies of a whole share; restore single files from them. Azure Backup can schedule snapshots for you.

callout.text: Soft delete protects against deletion; versioning and snapshots protect against overwrites.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Data protection
body: Recycle bin for deletes, versions for overwrites.
recap: Blob soft delete and container soft delete: 1–365 days
File share soft delete keeps deleted shares
Use lifecycle rules to clean up old versions

handsOn.title: Recover an overwritten blob and a deleted file
handsOn.cost: Cents. A few small files in a Standard LRS account cost almost nothing; delete the account at the end.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.
A storage account in rg-az104-lab: Standard performance, LRS redundancy, default settings. Name it st<yourinitials><number> (lowercase letters and numbers only, globally unique).

steps.do: Open the account > Data management > Data protection. Tick 'Enable versioning for blobs' and 'Enable soft delete for blobs' (7 days) and 'Enable soft delete for containers'. Save.
Create a container named budget. Upload a text file named plan.txt containing 'version one'.
Edit plan.txt on your PC to say 'version two' and upload it again with 'Overwrite if files already exist' ticked.

steps.see: Two versions. The older one is marked as a previous version.

steps.do: Select the older version > Make current version. Download plan.txt.
Delete plan.txt. Then turn on 'Show deleted blobs' in the container.
steps.see: plan.txt shown as deleted. Because versioning is on, open plan.txt > Versions, select the latest previous version and choose Make current version.
steps.tip: Without versioning you would use Undelete instead; with versioning on, you restore by promoting a version.

steps.do: Create a file share named team, upload a file, then open team > Snapshots > + Add snapshot.
Delete the file from the share. Open the snapshot, find the file and select Restore.
steps.see: The file is back in the share.

check: You restored an older version of a blob and a file from a share snapshot.
cleanup: When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
